The Celestial Dragons' slave collars and bubble helmets disgust the crew, Caesar Clown gasses children, and the gigantification experiments at Punk Hazard turn stomachs.
Nothing itches.
No tickling occurs.
Shanks's and Luffy's Conqueror's Haki knocks crowds unconscious, and Enel's lightning and the Marineford cannonade overwhelm the senses.
The crew climbs Drum Island's frozen mountain, crosses Alabasta's desert, splits between Punk Hazard's burning and frozen halves, and faces Aokiji's ice and Akainu's magma.
Usopp trembles before every giant foe, villagers cower under Arlong and Doflamingo, and even Luffy freezes when Kuma makes his crew vanish at Sabaody.
Nami hides her terror of Arlong for years, Robin lives in dread of another Buster Call, and Vivi frets over Alabasta's civil war.
The Straw Hats scatter in panic before Kizaru and Kuma at Sabaody, Enies Lobby burns under the Buster Call, and Luffy breaks down screaming after Ace dies.
Sanji's cooking, barrels of sake, Nami's hot baths, and the feast that ends every arc make the senses the crew's reward.
Brook's songs and Bink's Sake, Usopp's paintings and flags, Franky's Thousand Sunny, and the wonders of Skypiea and the Grand Line are savored.
Sanji's cooking is praised but spice is seldom the point; Luffy eats anything.
Luffy treats the Grand Line as a playground, chasing giant beetles, riding sea kings, playing with Chopper and Usopp, and whooping at every new island.
No sexual act occurs; Sanji's nosebleeds are as far as it goes.
Boa Hancock swoons for Luffy, who cares only for meat, Sanji courts every woman, and Oden's marriage to Toki anchors Wano's past.
Ace dies shielding Luffy, Bellemere dies for Nami and Nojiko, Sanji rejects the Vinsmokes and loves Zeff, and Momonosuke carries Oden's inheritance.
Luffy's grief at Ace's death breaks him, the crew weeps as the Going Merry burns, and every member carries a dead mentor or parent.
Brook wanders a ghost ship fifty years longing for his dead crew and for Laboon, and the Straw Hats spend two years apart aching to reunite.
Sanji's eyes turn to hearts and his nose bleeds at Nami, Robin, and the mermaids, and Absalom's lust for Nami is played for laughs.
The Straw Hats' friendship is the series' heart: Luffy declares war on the world for Robin, Zoro offers his life for Luffy's, and each recruitment is an act of friendship.
Luffy puts his hat on Nami's head when she finally cries for help, Chopper feels every patient's pain, and Robin reads the hurt in others.
Sanji feeds the starving pirate Gin, Chopper heals anyone, Luffy punches a Celestial Dragon to free a slave, and Corazon dies to cure Law.
Luffy carries Shanks's straw hat as a debt of gratitude, Vivi's farewell at Alabasta is thanks the crew answers with raised arms, and Law lives to repay Corazon.
Luffy saves kingdom after kingdom and refuses to be called a hero, Chopper beams when thanked, and Sanji feeds anyone who is hungry.
Luffy trusts Nami when she has just robbed them, the crew doubts Robin until Enies Lobby, Usopp lies for a living, and Kanjuro betrays the Wano alliance.
Luffy wants to die after Ace and is saved by Jinbe's reminder of his crew, and Robin wished to die until the crew made her shout that she wants to live.
Luffy's anger erupts when his crew or friends are hurt, from Arlong to Doflamingo to Kaido, and Sanji's and Zoro's at insults to the crew.
Buggy envies Shanks's rise, Blackbeard covets Whitebeard's power, and the Charlotte siblings compete for Big Mom's favor.
Boa Hancock seethes at any woman near Luffy, and Sanji sulks when Nami's attention goes elsewhere.
Usopp's quarrel with Luffy at Water 7 is partly fear of being left behind, and Carrot and Chopper squabble over Luffy's attention.
Hody Jones is built of hatred of humans, Arlong of humans too, Doflamingo of the world that cast him out, and the crew hates the Celestial Dragons.
The Celestial Dragons treat all others as insects, Doflamingo scorns the trash of Dressrosa, and Crocodile sneers at Luffy's dream.
Fisher Tiger's resentment of slavery, Wano's of Orochi's starvation regime, Dressrosa's of Doflamingo's toy curse, and Robin's of Ohara's destruction fuel every uprising.
Luffy declares he will be Pirate King, Zoro refuses to lose to anyone but Mihawk, and Whitebeard dies standing; pride is the pirate's creed.
Luffy's rubber faces, Usopp's lies, Sanji and Zoro's bickering, Brook's skull jokes, and Franky's poses keep the manga laughing between fights.
Each Straw Hat is an outcast, Chopper the monster reindeer, Robin the demon child, Brook the skeleton, who finds a crew to belong to.
Robin spent twenty years alone and hunted, Brook fifty years alone on a ghost ship, and Chopper was driven from his herd; loneliness is what the crew cures.
Akainu's Absolute Justice, the Buster Call on Ohara, Fujitora's shame at the Marines, and Luffy's refusal to let injustice stand make judgment constant.
Luffy worships Shanks, Coby and Bartolomeo idolize Luffy, Zoro reveres Mihawk, and the world speaks of Roger and Whitebeard with awe.
Chopper dances insisting compliments do not please him, Zoro gets lost walking in a straight line, and Sanji is mortified by his Okama training.
Zoro swears never to lose again after Mihawk, Usopp cannot face the crew after leaving, Sanji hides his Vinsmoke blood, and Nami weeps for her betrayal.
Luffy blames himself for Ace's death, Robin for Ohara's fate, Law for Corazon's, and Usopp for abandoning the crew.
Every arc ends in tears: Vivi's farewell, the Going Merry's last words, Chopper's doctor's cherry blossoms, and Brook's reunion with Laboon's memory.
The crew's days aboard the Sunny, fishing, feasting, and laughing, are the happiness that every arc restores.
Luffy roars with joy at every victory, feast, and new island, and the crew's parties shake the ship.
Luffy trains two years with Rayleigh, Zoro with Mihawk, and every climax turns on a hero refusing to fall.
Zoro's blade work and Luffy's Observation Haki in the fight with Katakuri show absorbed mastery, and Sanji in the kitchen is in his element.
Luffy gets bored on calm days at sea and pesters Usopp and Chopper for games.
Luffy is distracted by any meat or adventure in sight, and Zoro gets lost whenever he walks alone.
Luffy never waits for a plan, charges every stronghold head-on, and demands to set sail for the next island at once.
Luffy must see what every island holds, Robin hunts the Poneglyphs for the Void Century's truth, and the whole world asks what One Piece is.
Luffy learns his father is the revolutionary Dragon, Sabo turns up alive at Dressrosa, Sanji is a Vinsmoke prince, and plot twists land in every arc.
Whitebeard tilts the sea, Enel's ark rises to the moon, Zunesha the giant elephant walks the ocean, and Luffy gapes at every wonder.
Nobody believes Usopp's tales until they come true, the crew doubts Robin, and everyone laughs at the idea of a sky island.
Robin pieces together fragments of the Void Century, and Luffy recalls Shanks's words at crucial moments.
Luffy understands almost nothing anyone explains, the crew is lost in Skypiea's rules, and the mysteries of the Void Century baffle everyone.
Luffy reaches Ace and still loses him, cannot beat Crocodile twice, and Usopp rages at his own weakness.
Vivi chooses between crew and country, Usopp decides whether to come back, and Luffy is never uncertain about anything.
Robin's Poneglyph readings bring the world's hidden history into view, and Luffy, who understands little, understands his crew perfectly.
Luffy invents Gear Second from Lucci's speed, Usopp builds Pop Greens and the Kabuto, and Franky builds the Thousand Sunny.
Each arc ends with the villain beaten, the island freed, and a feast; the great goal of One Piece stays unfinished.
The Poneglyphs, the Will of D., and Whitebeard's dying promise that One Piece exists foreshadow the final war.
Every member's past is told in flashback, Brook sings Bink's Sake for a crew fifty years gone, and Luffy carries Shanks's hat from childhood.
Each fight and each island hangs on a cliffhanger, and the crew sails toward One Piece.
Luffy's dream of becoming Pirate King, each crewmate's dream, and the hope of the oppressed in every kingdom are the series' fuel.
The crew laughs at Buggy's humiliations, and Luffy's punch to a Celestial Dragon is savored by everyone who saw it.
Whitebeard dies standing for his sons, Oden boils for an hour to save his retainers, and Corazon gives his life for Law.
Boa Hancock is besotted with Luffy, and Sanji falls at the sight of every woman.
Luffy's rage at Ace's death, at Doflamingo's toys, and at Kaido's cruelty, and Akainu's fury, drive the greatest battles.
